title: Geometric Analysis of the Damped Harmonic Oscillator via the Lambert W Function
summary: The underdamped harmonic oscillator is analyzed through the complex mapping $ζ= e^{-i\varphi}we^{-w}$ with $w = βt + iΩt$, which transforms the dynamics into a logarithmic spiral. Within this framework, the displacement extrema correspond to crossings of the imaginary axis by $ζ(t)$, yielding the explicit times $t_n = (θ- \varphi - π/2 + nπ)/Ω$, where $θ= \arctan(Ω/β)$. The Lambert $W$ function provides closed-form solutions $t = -β^{-1}W_k(-βA/ω_0)$ for the times at which the spiral radius attains a given threshold $A$, covering both the rising and decaying branches.
